name: Hanoi food guide
summary: Pho in the Hoan Kiem lanes in the morning, bun cha at lunch, egg coffee in the afternoon, then snail noodles, young rice from Vong, sticky rice, and the rooms that cook in another register: a seasonal Vietnamese menu, a Japanese counter, Cantonese, and the white tablecloths at the Metropole.
body: Eat Hanoi from the bowl outward. The morning soup is pho. Lunch is bun cha. The afternoon sit-down is egg coffee, strong robusta under a sweet egg foam, in the Nguyen Huu Huan alley. Around those three, the city still cooks bun dau, cha ca finished at the table, shrimp cakes that take their name from West Lake, and a breakfast roll of steamed rice.

The photographs are those plates, plus banh mi, che, and goi cuon. The names under them are the other dishes Vietnam Tourism and the tourism center print: snail noodles, pillow cakes, young rice from Vong, sticky rice, crab noodles, fresh beer, and the rest. Walk the street the dish belongs to and read the board. Hours on those streets were not published. Check on arrival. When you want a room instead of a stool, the names below are the ones Vietnam Tourism and the 2025 MICHELIN Guide actually print. Hue’s bun bo is the bowl for the day you leave town.
specialtiesLead: Pho, bun cha, bun dau, cha ca, banh cuon, banh tom, bun thang, mi van than, mien luon, Vietnamese coffee, banh mi, che, and goi cuon have a photograph. The other names follow.

sections.heading: More Hanoi dishes
paragraphs: Vietnam Tourism and the tourism center name these dishes. Where an hour was not printed, the hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Mien
spots.note: Miến is chewy glass noodle made from mung bean or sweet potato, mild and savory, topped with chicken, crab, or freshwater eel, in broth or stir-fried. Vietnam Tourism’s ten-dish list points to a mixed bowl at 6 Phùng Hưng, Hoàn Kiếm. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Nom bo kho
spots.note: Nộm bò khô is a sweet and sour plate of green papaya, carrot, and beef jerky. One Hanoi page adds crunchy peanuts. A street-food walk adds lemon balm and fish sauce. 23 Hoàn Kiếm, the address on Vietnam Tourism’s ten-dish list. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bun ca
spots.note: Bún cá is fish with rice noodles. Vietnam Tourism’s ten-dish list makes it a sweet and sour summer bowl of fried tilapia, Vietnamese celery, pineapple, and tomato. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article describes a lunch bowl of fried fish with a green vegetable it compares to morning glory, plus cilantro and dill. Vietnam Tourism’s ten-dish list points to 14 Trung Yên alley, Hàng Bạc, Hoàn Kiếm. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article does not name a second door. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bun oc
spots.note: Bún ốc is snail rice vermicelli, one of Hanoi’s classic comfort bowls on Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article. The bowl has rice vermicelli, and the article names beef, crab meat, and herbs in a broth of tomatoes, wine vinegar, and pepper. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article does not name a street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Lau
spots.note: Lẩu is the hot pot on Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article: a bubbling pot you fill with fresh vegetables, meat, and seafood. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article does not name a street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh da tron
spots.note: Bánh đa trộn is thick, flat rice noodles topped with sausage, fried fish cakes, tofu, peanuts, and leafy vegetables. Vietnam Tourism calls it one of Hanoi’s specialties and says thin glass noodles, miến, are another option from the same baskets. Old Quarter, from the carrying pole Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article describes. A house number was not printed. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh goi
spots.note: Bánh gối is a pillow-shaped fried pastry. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article fills it with minced pork, black fungus, vermicelli, and a quail egg. A street-food walk fills it with pork, wood-ear mushrooms, and glass noodles, and does not mention the egg. Both articles set it in the Old Quarter walk. A house number was not printed. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: My ga tan
spots.note: Mỳ gà tần is braised chicken with egg noodles. Vietnam Tourism says the chicken, regular or the smaller black-skinned bird, is simmered in an empty drink can with herbs that include mugwort, then egg noodles go into the stew. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article does not name a street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh duc nong
spots.note: Bánh đúc nóng is a hot steamed cake of plain rice and tapioca flour. Vietnam Tourism fills it with black fungus, meat, and fried shallots, and serves it with chilli-garlic fish sauce and herbs. Vietnam Tourism’s stadium note names a bánh đúc door at 45 Châu Long, Quán Thánh, Ba Đình. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ha cao
spots.note: Há cảo, on Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article, is a fried dumpling sold with bánh gối. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article does not name a separate street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Pho mai que
spots.note: Phô mai que is a fried cheese stick. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article sells it with bánh gối. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article does not name a separate street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Nem chua ran
spots.note: Nem chua rán is fried fermented sausage. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article sells it with bánh gối. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi street-food article does not name a separate street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh khuc
spots.note: Bánh khúc is a Hanoi specialty on Vietnam Tourism’s street-food walk: roasted pork and mung-bean paste layered in sticky rice with khúc leaves from the Red River, steamed in banana leaves. A sidewalk vendor on the Old Quarter walk. A house number was not printed. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ca cuon thit
spots.note: Cá cuộn thịt is a fried fish ball stuffed with pork. Vietnam Tourism’s street-food walk serves it with fresh greens, a light fish sauce, and calamansi. An Old Quarter market corner. A street name was not printed. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bia hoi
spots.note: Bia hơi is Hanoi’s fresh draft beer. Vietnam Tourism says the beer is unpasteurized and drunk soon after it is made, and calls a glass as light as water. Tạ Hiện and Lương Ngọc Quyến, the beer corner the tourism pages name. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Pho cuon
spots.note: Phở cuốn is a roll wrapped in fresh rice-noodle sheets, the sheets usually cut into phở noodles, not dried rice paper. Vietnam Tourism says to look for grilled beef around Trúc Bạch. Ngũ Xã, Trúc Bạch. Vietnam Tourism’s rolls article says restaurants around the lake. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Com Vong
spots.note: Cốm Vòng is young green rice from Vòng village in Cầu Giấy. The tourism center says the grains are gently sweet, soft, and scented with lotus, and that the traditional pairing is ripe banana. Vòng village, Cầu Giấy ward. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh com
spots.note: Bánh cốm is a sweet rice cake filled with mung-bean paste, one of the cốm dishes the tourism center names from Vòng village. Vòng village, Cầu Giấy. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Che com
spots.note: Chè cốm is a sweet soup made from young green rice. The tourism center names it with the other dishes from cốm Vòng. Vòng village, Cầu Giấy. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Cha com
spots.note: Chả cốm is a pork patty made with young green rice. The tourism center names it among the dishes from cốm Vòng. Vòng village, Cầu Giấy. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Xoi
spots.note: Xôi is dense sticky rice, savoury or sweet. Vietnam Tourism calls savoury xôi mặn an inexpensive breakfast and says there are more than 20 sweet kinds. The Hanoi door on that list is Xôi Yến. Xôi Yến, 35B Nguyễn Hữu Huân, Lý Thái Tổ, Hoàn Kiếm. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bun rieu
spots.note: Bún riêu is a crab and tomato noodle soup. Vietnam Tourism describes slippery rice noodles, fresh crab, tofu, and stewed tomatoes in an acidic broth, with clusters of minced crab, ground pork, and egg. Bún Riêu Cua Thanh Hồng, 42 Hòa Mã, Ngô Thì Nhậm, Hai Bà Trưng. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bun ngan
spots.note: Bún ngan is a noodle soup of bamboo shoots and duck meat. Vietnam Tourism names it among the Vietnamese classics around Quần Ngựa in Ba Đình. The same note names Hạnh Bún Miến Ngan at 63 Cửa Bắc, Quán Thánh, Ba Đình. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bit tet
spots.note: Bít tết is a Vietnamese steak in the French style. Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi interview places it on Hòe Nhai. Hòe Nhai. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ice cream
spots.note: An ice-cream cone on Tràng Tiền is the evening walk around Hoàn Kiếm. Vietnam Tourism calls that cone an essential Hanoi habit. Tràng Tiền. Vietnam Tourism’s Old Quarter article puts the walk in the evening. The clock is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Rice wine
spots.note: Rượu on Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi weekend is a spirit made from sticky rice and flavoured with local fruits. A street-food article on the same site also describes rice wine with passionfruit and apple. Highway 4, the door on Vietnam Tourism’s weekend itinerary, which says the bar has four locations. Vietnam Tourism’s street-food walk does not name its bistro. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Quay
spots.note: Quẩy is the fried breadstick Vietnam Tourism says Hanoi eats with most noodles. Dip it in the broth. With the noodle bowls. The miến door on Vietnam Tourism’s ten-dish list is 6 Phùng Hưng, Hoàn Kiếm. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: International dining
paragraphs: Vietnam Tourism’s Hanoi dining page names three foreign kitchens, and an interview on the same site names a Vietnamese steak in the French style on Hòe Nhai. Hours were not published. Check on arrival.

spots.name: Crystal Jade Palace
spots.note: Cantonese cooking from a Singapore kitchen that Vietnam Tourism says has served Chinese food in Vietnam for 25 years. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Kappou Ishia
spots.note: A Japanese omakase. The page describes 10 courses: appetizers, sashimi, a main, rice, and a dessert, chosen by the chef. The same article’s credit spells the room Kappou Ishida. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Hibana by Koki
spots.note: A 14-seat teppanyaki counter in the basement of Capella Hanoi. Chef Hiroshi Yamaguchi. Vietnam Tourism names abalone, spiny lobster, sea urchin, Yaeyama beef, and Hokkaido hairy crab among the ingredients. One MICHELIN Star, retained in the 2025 selection. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: The casual city is the morning street, the lunch street, the alley coffee, and the bia hơi corner at Tạ Hiện and Lương Ngọc Quyến. A gate fee is not published for these streets. Check on arrival if someone asks for one.
Đồng Xuân is the covered market in the lanes. Entry is free. The hours are Check on arrival. It is the shopping hall beside the food.

spots.name: Hang Vai
spots.note: The morning pho street, with the lanes around Hoàn Kiếm. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Cua Dong
spots.note: The lunch street for bun cha. Put the noodles in with the herbs. Nem is optional.

spots.name: Ma May
spots.note: The bun dau lane in the Old Quarter. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Duong Thanh
spots.note: The cha ca street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Cafe Giang
spots.note: The afternoon alley for egg coffee. The tourism pages name Café Giảng as the door. The clock is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ta Hien corner
spots.address: Tạ Hiện and Lương Ngọc Quyến
spots.note: The bia hơi corner north of the lake. Stools, draft beer, and the street. No drink price is printed here. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Dinh Cafe
spots.note: Second floor of an old French house looking onto Hoàn Kiếm. The interview calls it a classic cafe. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Pho Co Cafe
spots.note: A hidden cafe the interview names at 11 Hàng Gai. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Pho Co Rooftop Cafe
spots.note: A rooftop over the tube houses, with a view of Hoàn Kiếm. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Nola Cafe
spots.note: The interview puts a gallery on top, looking down into the oldest house on the street. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ha Thanh Mansion
spots.note: New to the 2025 Bib Gourmand list. Michelin describes a century-old villa of three floors. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Hang Dao night market
spots.note: On weekend nights Hàng Đào becomes a market for snail meatballs, grilled quail, and cured pork sausage. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Dong Xuan
spots.note: The covered market in the lanes. Entry is free. The hours are Check on arrival.

spots.name: Pho Bo Lam
spots.note: New to the 2025 Bib Gourmand list. Michelin names the beef heel muscle, with tender meat and gelatinous tendon. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Pho Au Trieu
spots.note: On the 2024 Bib Gourmand list, on a street parallel to St Joseph’s Cathedral. The tour calls the broth cloudy, fatty, and thick, in the Nam Định style, and says the shop can sell out. Go early. A closing hour is not printed.

spots.name: Bun Cha Huong Lien
spots.note: In 2015 Barack Obama and Anthony Bourdain ate here. The table may have been put behind glass. On the 2025 MICHELIN Selected list. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Tuyet Bun Cha 34
spots.note: A 2024 Bib Gourmand room near Trúc Bạch, Trần Quốc, and Quán Thánh. The tour describes generous noodles, grilled pork, and herbs. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Cha Ca Thang Long
spots.note: The Michelin city tour ends the day here, with the fish cooked at the table. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh Cuon Ba Xuan
spots.note: The Michelin city tour names this room for breakfast banh cuon on the second day. On the 2025 MICHELIN Selected list. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Mien Luon Chan Cam
spots.note: New to the 2025 Bib Gourmand list. Nearly 40 years in the Old Quarter. Eel cold or stir-fried, vermicelli soup, congee, and spring rolls. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Mien Luon Dong Thinh
spots.note: The 2024 tour’s eel shop, a Bib Gourmand, described as more than four decades of glass noodles with eel, greens, crushed peanuts, and fried shallots. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Mau Dich So 37
spots.note: New to the 2025 Bib Gourmand list. Michelin describes a rustic room and names Hanoi spring rolls, fried hemibagrus, and scorched rice with beef stew. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Uu Dam
spots.note: New to the 2025 Bib Gourmand list. A vegetarian menu Michelin calls traditional and balanced. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Oc Di Tu
spots.note: On the 2025 MICHELIN Selected list. The city tour describes prawns, clams, and cockles in a plain room, and names melo melo snails with scallion and fried garlic, and Venus clams with lemongrass, chili, and pineapple. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Fine dining
paragraphs: Hanoi’s one-star rooms in the 2025 MICHELIN selection are Gia, Hibana by Koki, and Tầm Vị. Lamai Garden received the city’s first Green Star the same year. Spices Garden is the Metropole dining room Vietnam Tourism files with the foreign kitchens. Vietnam Tourism’s weekend itinerary prints a buffet lunch there at 780,000 VND. No hour was printed for these rooms, and the other rooms have no price printed. Check on arrival.

spots.name: Gia
spots.note: Vietnamese contemporary cooking. The menu changes with the seasons and draws on Vietnamese culinary heritage. Vietnam Tourism notes acidity and texture in the plates. One MICHELIN Star, retained in 2025. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Lamai Garden
spots.note: Reimagined in 2022 by chef-owner Hieu Trung Tran. A seasonal tasting menu and a vegetarian menu, contemporary Vietnamese and farm-to-table. Diners walk a garden to a counter by the open kitchen. Ingredients come from the restaurant’s Phú Thọ farm: herbs, ducks, and black pigs. Michelin names a squid noodle inspired by phở chua. MICHELIN Green Star, 2025. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Tam Vi
spots.note: Northern Vietnamese cooking in a vintage tea house, with old furniture and handwritten signs. Vietnam Tourism names chả ốc with herbs, vegetables, rice vermicelli, and fish sauce, and a clear crab soup with malabar spinach. One MICHELIN Star, retained in 2025. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Spices Garden
spots.note: The Metropole dining room. Vietnam Tourism says bun cha, pho, and cha ca are cooked with European technique and served on white tablecloths. The weekend itinerary prints a buffet lunch at 780,000 VND. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Themed dining
paragraphs: Chim Sáo is a French villa where the staff dress in old peasant clothes and the cooking is home food.

spots.name: Chim Sao
spots.note: A French villa. The interview says the staff dress in old-style peasant clothes and the food is home cooking. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Breakfast is pho in the Hoàn Kiếm lanes, banh cuon across the city and at Bánh Cuốn Bà Xuân, bun thang, and xôi mặn, the savoury sticky rice Vietnam Tourism calls an inexpensive breakfast. Phở cuốn is the grilled-beef roll on Ngũ Xã, by Trúc Bạch, and the weekend itinerary places that stop in the evening. Bun cha is almost only lunch. The morning clock is Check on arrival.

seoTitle: Hanoi food — pho, bun cha, cafes, and fine dining
seoDescription: Morning pho in the Hoan Kiem lanes, bun cha at lunch around Cua Dong, egg coffee in the Nguyen Huu Huan alley, and the other Hanoi dishes Vietnam Tourism names.
